daemons_bindKeyDaemonPollHelp: This daemon authenticates with a key that isn't bound to it. Binding a key gives it a dedicated credential that can be managed independently from other keys. Once you do, you'll get a command to run on the daemon machine to switch it over; until then it keeps working on its current key.

daemons_bindKeyServerPollWarning: This daemon authenticates with a key that isn't bound to it. Binding a key gives it a dedicated credential that can be managed independently from other keys. Because the daemon is in ServerPoll mode, binding a key will cause the server to use the new key to connect to the daemon immediately. You'll need to update the daemon with the new key for it to continue working, so only do this when you can reconfigure it right away.

meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_descri: Discover Docker containers and the services they expose. Connects over TCP, optionally with TLS.
meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_path_h: Optional URL path prefix appended after the port
meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_port_h: Docker API port. Use 2375 for non-TLS proxies (Tecnativa, HAProxy) or 2376 for TLS.
meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_ssl_ce: PEM-encoded client certificate. All three TLS fields (cert, key, CA chain) must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_ssl_ch: PEM-encoded CA certificate chain. All three TLS fields must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_DockerProxy_ssl_ke: PEM private key. All three TLS fields must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_DockerSocket_descr: Discover Docker containers and the services they expose. Connects via the daemon's local socket.
meta_credential_types_DockerSocket_socke: Path to the Docker Unix socket. Leave blank to auto-detect (DOCKER_HOST or /var/run/docker.sock).
meta_credential_types_Gnmi_description: Discover a host's interfaces and LLDP neighbors over gNMI (OpenConfig). Connects over gRPC; username and password travel as request metadata.
meta_credential_types_Gnmi_port_helpText: 9339 is the IANA gNMI port; some NOSes listen on 6030 or 57400 instead.
meta_credential_types_Gnmi_username_help: Sent as gRPC `username` metadata (the OpenConfig convention).
meta_credential_types_InstantOnAccount_d: Discover Instant On switches, access points and gateways, their ports, the uplinks between them, and the MACs attached to each port. Connects to the Instant On cloud portal with a site account.
meta_credential_types_InstantOnAccount_s: Limit the fetch to one Instant On site by name. Leave blank to read every site this account can see. Assign this credential to a single switch — each host it is assigned to fetches the whole site again.
meta_credential_types_InstantOnAccount_u: Email address of an Instant On portal account with access to the site. Add a dedicated account with the read-only Viewer role (Site management → Accounts managing this site) rather than using your own administrator login, and make sure multi-factor authentication is disabled on it — the sign-in cannot answer an MFA prompt.
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_descri: Discover Podman containers and the services they expose. Connects over TCP, optionally with TLS.
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_path_h: Optional URL path prefix appended after the port
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_port_h: Podman API port. Point at a TCP-exposed Podman service (e.g. `podman system service tcp:`) directly or behind a TLS proxy.
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_ssl_ce: PEM-encoded client certificate. All three TLS fields (cert, key, CA chain) must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_ssl_ch: PEM-encoded CA certificate chain. All three TLS fields must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_PodmanProxy_ssl_ke: PEM private key. All three TLS fields must be provided together.
meta_credential_types_PodmanSocket_descr: Discover Podman containers and the services they expose. Connects via the daemon's local socket.
meta_credential_types_PodmanSocket_socke: Path to the Podman Unix socket. Leave blank to auto-detect (rootful /run/podman/podman.sock or the rootless $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock).
meta_credential_types_SnmpV1_community_h: Custom SNMP community string. The default 'public' community is always tried automatically during scans. On Cisco switches, append '@' and a VLAN id — for example 'readonly@20' — to read that VLAN's MAC-address table, which the plain community does not return.
meta_credential_types_SnmpV1_description: Discover a host's interfaces, system details, and CDP/LLDP neighbors. Uses SNMPv1.
meta_credential_types_SnmpV2c_community_: Custom SNMP community string. The default 'public' community is always tried automatically during scans. On Cisco switches, append '@' and a VLAN id — for example 'readonly@20' — to read that VLAN's MAC-address table, which the plain community does not return.
meta_credential_types_SnmpV2c_descriptio: Discover a host's interfaces, system details, and CDP/LLDP neighbors. Uses SNMPv2c.
meta_credential_types_SnmpV3_context_nam: Optional SNMPv3 context name, applied to bridge and VLAN queries only. Cisco and some other vendors keep a separate MAC-address table per VLAN in a named context; naming it here reads that table instead of the near-empty default one. Interface, LLDP and ARP data always come from the default context.
meta_credential_types_SnmpV3_description: Discover a host's interfaces, system details, and CDP/LLDP neighbors. Uses SNMPv3.
meta_credential_types_UnifiApiKey_api_ke: Network Application API key (Settings → Control Plane → Integrations → Create API Key). Requires UniFi OS; the legacy self-hosted Network Application on 8443 has no API keys — use a UniFi Local Admin credential there instead.
meta_credential_types_UnifiApiKey_descri: Discover UniFi-managed switches, access points and gateways, their ports, and the LLDP neighbors and uplinks the controller sees. Connects with a controller API key. Requires UniFi OS; the legacy self-hosted Network Application does not support API keys.
meta_credential_types_UnifiApiKey_port_h: 443 for a UniFi OS console (Dream Machine, Cloud Key, Cloud Gateway), 11443 for a self-hosted UniFi OS Server, or 8443 for the legacy self-hosted Network Application. Check the port in your controller's URL — the wrong port fails to connect.
meta_credential_types_UnifiApiKey_site_h: Internal site name, taken from the controller URL (/manage/site/<name>) — not the site's display name. Most installations use 'default'.
meta_credential_types_UnifiLocalAdmin_de: Discover UniFi-managed switches, access points and gateways, their ports, and the LLDP neighbors and uplinks the controller sees. Connects with a local admin account. Works with every controller, including the legacy self-hosted Network Application.
meta_credential_types_UnifiLocalAdmin_pa: Password for the local admin account.
meta_credential_types_UnifiLocalAdmin_po: 443 for a UniFi OS console (Dream Machine, Cloud Key, Cloud Gateway), 11443 for a self-hosted UniFi OS Server, or 8443 for the legacy self-hosted Network Application. Check the port in your controller's URL — the wrong port fails to connect.
meta_credential_types_UnifiLocalAdmin_si: Internal site name, taken from the controller URL (/manage/site/<name>) — not the site's display name. Most installations use 'default'.
meta_credential_types_UnifiLocalAdmin_us: Controller admin username. Use a local-only admin account so multi-factor authentication does not block the login.

meta_scan_settings_arp_scan_cutoff_helpT: Interfaced subnets larger than this CIDR prefix are truncated during ARP scanning. Lower values scan more IPs — increase ARP Scan Rate accordingly for large subnets.
meta_scan_settings_full_scan_interval_he: Run a full 65k port scan every N scans. Other scans use a lighter port set for faster results. Set to 0 for light scans only, 1 for every scan to be full.
meta_scan_settings_max_discovery_duratio: Hard time limit for a single discovery run, in seconds (default 21600 = 6 hours). When reached, the run stops and any hosts not yet scanned are left for the next run. Raise this for very large networks that need a longer window.
meta_scan_settings_port_scan_batch_size_: Ports scanned concurrently per host. Range: 16-1000.
meta_scan_settings_probe_raw_socket_port: Scan ports 9100-9107. May cause ghost printing on some printers.
meta_scan_settings_scan_rate_pps_helpTex: Probes per second during port scanning. Lower values reduce network impact.
meta_scan_settings_use_npcap_arp_helpTex: Use Npcap broadcast ARP instead of Windows SendARP. Requires Npcap installed.

meta_warning_codes_ClaimedCapabilityEmpt: {address} advertises {source}, but returned no {group} at all. A device that says it does this and then reports none of it is usually restricting what the credential may see — an SNMP view, or a VLAN context the query has to name.
meta_warning_codes_ClaimedCapabilityRead: {address} advertises {source}, and the read of its {group} ended without returning any. The incomplete-walk line for this device says why it ended; what the device advertises is why it is worth reading again rather than treating as empty.
meta_warning_codes_ClaimedCountReadCutSh: {address} reports {source} as {expected}, and the read ended at {observed} without finishing. That is how much of the table is missing — the incomplete-walk line for this device says why it ended. What was read is recorded.
meta_warning_codes_ClaimedCountUnderRead: {address} reports {source} as {expected}, but only {observed} could be read. What was read is recorded; the device may be misreporting its own count, or may be declining to serve the rest of the table to this credential.
Fewer rows than the device claims
meta_warning_codes_CredentialCollectionF: The {credential} credential for {address} authenticated and then failed while collecting, so this host's data is missing rather than out of date. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialCollectionT: The {credential} credential for {address} authenticated and then ran out of time before it finished collecting — rescan this host on its own, or narrow what the scan covers. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialGateClosed_: The {credential} credential for {address} was not tried because port {ports} was not open on it — check the port configured on the credential.
meta_warning_codes_CredentialMalformed_d: The {credential} credential for {address} is incomplete and could not be used — re-enter it. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialNotThisServ: The {credential} credential for {address} reached something that is not the expected service — check the port on the credential. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialRejected_de: The {credential} credential for {address} was refused — check the username, password or community string. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialTargetNotRe: The {credential} credential for {address} was not tried because nothing answered at that address during the scan — check the address is right and the host is online.
meta_warning_codes_CredentialTargetNotSc: The {credential} credential for {address} was never contacted because its address is not on any subnet this scan covers — add the subnet to the discovery, or move the credential to a host inside it.
meta_warning_codes_CredentialTimedOut_de: The {credential} credential for {address} timed out before anything answered — check the address and port, and that the service is listening rather than dropping the connection. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialTlsFailed_d: The {credential} credential for {address} could not negotiate TLS — if the appliance serves a self-signed certificate, turn on "accept invalid certificates" in the daemon's scan settings. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_CredentialUnreachable: The {credential} credential for {address} could not be reached at that address — check the address, port and that the service is listening. ({detail})
meta_warning_codes_InterfaceDetailsCutSh: {addresses} returned every SNMP interface but stopped while reading their details, so some descriptions or speeds may be blank.
meta_warning_codes_InterfaceSetCutShort_: {addresses} stopped responding partway through the SNMP interface list, so some interfaces are missing.
meta_warning_codes_LldpLocalPortDropped_: {addresses} reported LLDP neighbours on a local port that matches no interface on the device ({dropped} of {total}), so they are discarded and draw no links — those devices will look as though they have no LLDP neighbours. This usually means the switch numbers its LLDP ports separately from its interfaces, or did not answer for its LLDP port table.
meta_warning_codes_LldpLocalPortMisplace: {addresses} reported LLDP neighbours whose local port could not be identified but does match an interface number ({misplaced} in total), so they are drawn against a port that may not be the right one.
meta_warning_codes_LldpNeighbourAmbiguou: LLDP/CDP neighbours advertise an identifier that several hosts on this network hold ({count} in total), so none of them can be picked and no link is drawn. This is usually duplicate records for one device rather than a device that was missed. {examples}
meta_warning_codes_LldpNeighbourNotFound: LLDP/CDP neighbours name devices this network has not discovered ({count} in total), so they draw no links. This is expected where the far end is an endpoint or unmanaged device; a device that should have been scanned means the identifier it advertises is not one this network holds. {examples}
meta_warning_codes_LldpPortAmbiguous_des: LLDP/CDP neighbours resolved to a device but several of its ports match the advertised port id ({count} in total), so it identifies none and Physical Topology draws a dashed device-level link instead of a port-to-port one. {examples}
meta_warning_codes_LldpPortNoStrategy_de: LLDP/CDP neighbours resolved to a device but advertise a port id of a subtype there is no lookup for ({count} in total), so Physical Topology draws a dashed device-level link instead of a port-to-port one. {examples}
meta_warning_codes_LldpPortNoStrategy_na: No lookup for the advertised port id
meta_warning_codes_LldpPortNotFound_desc: LLDP/CDP neighbours resolved to a device but no port on it matches the advertised port id ({count} in total), so Physical Topology draws a dashed device-level link instead of a port-to-port one. {examples}
meta_warning_codes_MalformedNeighboursGh: {addresses} reported neighbour records without the identifier needed to match the far end ({discarded} in total), so {consequence}. The rows appeared only in the columns describing each neighbour, never in the one identifying it, so there was no identifier to lose. Rescanning will not change this.
meta_warning_codes_MalformedNeighboursIn: {addresses} reported neighbour records without the identifier needed to match the far end ({discarded} in total), so {consequence}. These neighbours were listed and then no identifier was supplied for them. The read finished, so rescanning will not change this.
meta_warning_codes_MalformedNeighboursUn: {addresses} reported neighbour records without the identifier needed to match the far end ({discarded} in total), so {consequence}. The identifying column came back with a value of a type it cannot hold. Rescanning will not change this.
Neighbour identifier of the wrong type

{addresses} reported neighbour records without the identifier needed to match the far end ({discarded} in total), so {consequence}. Their position in the neighbour table could not be read, so they could not be tied to a local port. Rescanning will not change this.
meta_warning_codes_MalformedNeighboursWa: {addresses} reported neighbour records without the identifier needed to match the far end ({discarded} in total), so {consequence}. The read of the column identifying the far end stopped before its end, so these records may come back on the next complete scan.
meta_warning_codes_ScanTimeLimitWithEsti: Scan hit its time limit ({hours}h) — {hosts_not_scanned} host(s) not scanned (~{minutes_remaining} min of estimated work remaining). Raise Max Discovery Duration or rescan.
meta_warning_codes_ScanTimeLimit_descrip: Scan hit its time limit ({hours}h) — {hosts_not_scanned} host(s) not scanned. Raise Max Discovery Duration or rescan.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpCollectedNothing_: {addresses} answered SNMP but returned no interfaces, neighbours, addresses or forwarding data at all. The credential is working, so this is either a device that implements nothing beyond its system description, or one whose tables could not be read — the daemon log records which for each table.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkBridgeMibAbse: {addresses} did not answer for {groups}, which these switches commonly do not implement. Their MAC-address-table and VLAN membership cannot be read over SNMP; a UniFi controller integration reports the same data where one manages the device.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkDesynchronise: {addresses} answered out of step with what was asked for {groups}, which usually means the agent is under load. Previously discovered values were kept and refresh on the next complete scan.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkEntryCap_desc: {addresses} has more {groups} than one scan reads — collection stops at {limit} entries per table, so the rest were not read. The data recorded is correct as far as it goes.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkEntryCap_name: Table larger than one scan reads
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkNoAnswer_desc: {addresses} returned no {groups} data at all — the device stopped answering rather than reporting that it has none. Previously discovered values were kept rather than overwritten and refresh on the next complete scan.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkPartialDiscar: {addresses} did not finish reporting {groups}, so what it did answer was not recorded — a partial read cannot tell a value that has gone from one that was not reached. Previously discovered values were kept, and refresh on the next complete scan.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkPartialRecord: {addresses} did not finish reporting {groups}, so what it read was recorded and the rest refreshes on the next complete scan.
meta_warning_codes_SnmpWalkUnsupported_d: {addresses} does not implement {groups} over SNMP, so it cannot be read from the device at all. Previously discovered values were kept.
meta_warning_codes_VlanRecordingFailed_d: The VLANs reported by {addresses} could not be saved, so VLAN membership is missing from their interfaces. The devices answered correctly — this is a failure recording the result, and the daemon log has the underlying error.
meta_warning_codes_WarningsTruncated_des: {elided} further warnings from this scan were not recorded, because it produced more than the scan record holds. Narrow what the scan covers to see the rest.
